restrictions.rule: Special events hosted on premises require appropriate permits and additional temporary security measures.
restrictions.why: To manage increased risk and ensure compliance with local regulations during high-traffic events.

restrictions.rule: Businesses must maintain up-to-date inventory management systems and conduct regular audits.
restrictions.why: To detect and address discrepancies promptly, reducing the likelihood of undetected loss.

restrictions.rule: Retailers must comply with all applicable copyright, licensing, and business operation laws.
restrictions.why: To avoid legal exposure and maintain eligibility for coverage.

restrictions.rule: Locations in high-crime areas must implement enhanced security protocols, such as reinforced entry points and additional surveillance.
restrictions.why: To mitigate elevated risk associated with the location.

restrictions.rule: Businesses with a loss history must provide evidence of corrective actions and ongoing monitoring.
restrictions.why: To demonstrate proactive risk management and reduce the likelihood of repeat incidents.

restrictions.rule: Online operations must have secure payment processing and data protection measures in place.
restrictions.why: To protect customer information and prevent cyber-related losses.

restrictions.rule: All premises must have adequate interior and exterior lighting during operating hours.
restrictions.why: To deter criminal activity and ensure safety for customers and staff.

preferred: Businesses with robust cyber hygiene practices, including regular vulnerability assessments and employee cybersecurity training, as this reduces the risk of data breaches.
Operations that maintain clear separation from media production and broadcasting activities, ensuring risk exposure remains within web design and online services.
Businesses with comprehensive professional liability (E&O) coverage in place, minimizing exposure to claims from professional errors.
Companies that use reputable, up-to-date software and development tools, lowering the risk of cyber incidents due to outdated technology.
Firms with documented data privacy and protection policies compliant with GDPR, CCPA, or other relevant regulations, demonstrating regulatory awareness.
Businesses that utilize secure cloud hosting providers with strong security certifications (e.g., ISO 27001), reducing infrastructure-related risks.
Operations that require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all remote access and critical systems, strengthening access controls.
Companies that conduct regular client communication and maintain clear project documentation, reducing the likelihood of misunderstandings and disputes.
Businesses that have incident response and business continuity plans in place, ensuring preparedness for cyber events or service interruptions.
Firms that restrict access to sensitive client data on a need-to-know basis, minimizing internal data exposure.
Operations that do not accept or process cryptocurrency payments, avoiding emerging risks in digital financial transactions.
Businesses that regularly review and update their risk management strategies in response to evolving industry threats.
Companies that utilize project management software with secure collaboration features, supporting secure workflow management.
Firms that have not experienced a significant cyber incident or professional liability claim in the past three years.
Businesses that provide ongoing staff training on regulatory compliance and data privacy requirements.
acceptable: Businesses with basic cyber hygiene measures in place, such as antivirus software and firewalls, but lacking advanced controls.
Operations that occasionally subcontract specialized work, provided subcontractors are vetted and insured.
Companies that use mainstream content management systems (CMS) with regular security updates.
Firms that have professional liability coverage but may need increased limits or broader coverage.
Businesses that primarily serve local or regional clients, limiting exposure to international regulatory requirements.
Operations that use third-party hosting providers with standard security protocols.
Companies that have experienced minor, non-systemic cyber incidents but have remediated vulnerabilities.
Firms that accept online payments through established, PCI-compliant processors.
Businesses that have a mix of remote and in-office staff, provided secure remote access protocols are enforced.
Operations that provide digital marketing services as an adjunct to web design, but do not engage in media production.
Companies that are in the process of updating their data privacy policies to meet new regulations.
Firms that use open-source development tools with active security support.
Businesses that have some documentation gaps in project management but are working to improve processes.
Operations that occasionally work with nonprofit or educational clients with higher data sensitivity, provided enhanced controls are in place.
Companies that are monitoring but not currently integrating emerging technologies such as AI or blockchain.
not_acceptable: Businesses involved in media production, such as video or audio content creation, due to increased liability and copyright risks.
Operations engaged in broadcasting activities, including streaming or live event production.
Companies that accept or process cryptocurrency payments, due to the volatility and regulatory uncertainty of digital currencies.
Firms lacking basic cyber hygiene controls, such as firewalls, antivirus, or secure passwords.
Businesses with a history of significant, unresolved cyber incidents or data breaches.
Operations that do not carry professional liability (E&O) insurance.
Companies that fail to comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
Firms that store sensitive client data without encryption or access controls.
Businesses that outsource core web development functions to unvetted or uninsured third parties.
Operations that have experienced multiple professional liability claims in the past three years.
Companies that do not have incident response or business continuity plans.
Firms that provide services to high-risk industries (e.g., adult content, gambling) without enhanced controls.
Businesses that lack clear operational boundaries between web design and prohibited activities.
Operations that use unsupported or obsolete software for client projects.
Companies that have been subject to regulatory enforcement actions for data privacy violations.

restrictions.rule: Exclude businesses engaged in media production activities.
restrictions.why: Media production introduces additional liability and copyright risks outside the scope of web design.

restrictions.rule: Exclude businesses engaged in broadcasting activities.
restrictions.why: Broadcasting presents unique regulatory and operational risks not covered by standard web design policies.

restrictions.rule: Restrict coverage for businesses accepting or processing cryptocurrency payments.
restrictions.why: Cryptocurrency transactions carry emerging risks and regulatory uncertainty.

restrictions.rule: Require evidence of strong cyber hygiene practices for all applicants.
restrictions.why: Weak cyber controls significantly increase the risk of data breaches and cyber incidents.

restrictions.rule: Decline businesses lacking professional liability (E&O) coverage.
restrictions.why: Professional liability insurance is essential to mitigate risks from errors and omissions.

restrictions.rule: Scrutinize businesses with a history of significant cyber incidents or professional liability claims.
restrictions.why: Past incidents may indicate ongoing vulnerabilities or operational weaknesses.

restrictions.rule: Exclude businesses that fail to comply with data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA).
restrictions.why: Non-compliance exposes the business to regulatory penalties and reputational harm.

restrictions.rule: Restrict coverage for businesses storing sensitive client data without encryption.
restrictions.why: Unencrypted data storage increases the risk of data loss and regulatory violations.

restrictions.rule: Monitor and review the impact of emerging technologies (e.g., AI, blockchain) on risk exposure.
restrictions.why: New technologies may introduce unforeseen risks that require updated underwriting guidelines.

restrictions.rule: Require clear operational boundaries to exclude prohibited activities.
restrictions.why: Ambiguous operations may inadvertently include higher-risk activities.

restrictions.rule: Assess adequacy of incident response and business continuity plans.
restrictions.why: Preparedness for cyber events is critical to minimize operational disruption.

restrictions.rule: Decline businesses with unresolved regulatory enforcement actions.
restrictions.why: Regulatory issues indicate potential ongoing compliance failures.

preferred: Businesses operating solely as wedding planners with no direct ownership or operation of physical venues; lower exposure to property and liability risks.
Wedding service providers offering off-site coordination only, with no responsibility for food, alcohol, or on-site event management.
Home-based wedding consultants with no client meetings or events held at their residence.
Businesses that subcontract all catering, floral, and entertainment services to licensed third parties, reducing direct liability.
Providers specializing in virtual or remote wedding planning services, with no physical event involvement.
Photographers or videographers specializing in weddings, operating from a studio with no on-site hosting or catering.
Businesses with a documented history of no claims or losses in the past five years.
Wedding service providers with written contracts outlining clear limits of liability and client responsibilities.
acceptable: Small wedding chapels hosting ceremonies only, with no on-site receptions or alcohol service.
Florists or decorators providing services exclusively for weddings, with no installation of large structures or use of open flames.
Businesses operating in commercial venues with up-to-date fire and safety inspections.
Wedding planners who occasionally coordinate on-site events but do not provide catering or alcohol.
Providers who require all vendors (caterers, bakers, musicians) to carry their own insurance.
Businesses with a formal risk management plan addressing crowd control, emergency exits, and weather contingencies.
Wedding service providers with seasonal operations, demonstrating off-season risk mitigation strategies.
Businesses that limit event size to under 100 attendees per event.
Providers who use only licensed and inspected rental equipment for events.
Businesses with staff trained in basic first aid and emergency procedures.
Wedding chapels with no overnight accommodations or lodging services.
Providers who do not allow fireworks, pyrotechnics, or open flames as part of ceremonies.
Businesses that do not offer transportation services as part of their packages.
Wedding service providers with a clear cancellation and refund policy in place.
not_acceptable: Wedding chapels or venues that host receptions with on-site alcohol service or operate as bars/nightclubs.
Businesses providing catering services without proper food handling permits or health inspections.
Operations that host events exceeding 300 attendees at any time.
Businesses that allow or provide pyrotechnics, fireworks, or open flames as part of ceremonies or receptions.
Wedding venues offering overnight accommodations, such as bed & breakfast or hotel operations.
Providers who own or operate transportation services, including limousines or shuttle buses.
Businesses with a history of claims related to property damage, bodily injury, or liquor liability in the past three years.
Operations located in residential areas without proper zoning or event permits.
Businesses that construct or install temporary structures (e.g., large tents, stages) without licensed contractors.
Providers offering adventure or destination weddings involving high-risk activities (e.g., skydiving, boating, remote locations).
Wedding service providers who serve or allow cannabis or other controlled substances at events.
Businesses that do not require written contracts or waivers for all clients and vendors.
Operations with no formal risk management or emergency response plan.
Providers who allow unsupervised minors or children’s parties as part of their services.
Businesses operating in areas with a history of frequent natural disasters without adequate contingency planning.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses providing or serving alcohol on premises.
restrictions.why: Alcohol service significantly increases liability exposure and is outside underwriting appetite.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for venues offering overnight accommodations.
restrictions.why: Lodging operations introduce additional property and liability risks not contemplated in this class.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for events exceeding 300 attendees.
restrictions.why: Large gatherings increase risk of crowd control issues, property damage, and bodily injury.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses operating without required local permits or licenses.
restrictions.why: Unlicensed operations are non-compliant and present unmanageable regulatory risks.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses with a history of claims or losses in the past three years.
restrictions.why: Recent claims history indicates higher risk profile.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses providing transportation services.
restrictions.why: Transportation introduces auto liability exposures not covered under this policy.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses constructing or installing temporary structures without licensed contractors.
restrictions.why: Improperly installed structures can lead to significant property and injury claims.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses allowing fireworks, pyrotechnics, or open flames.
restrictions.why: These activities present severe fire and injury hazards.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses operating in residential areas without proper zoning.
restrictions.why: Non-compliance with zoning laws can result in legal and regulatory action.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses without a formal risk management or emergency response plan.
restrictions.why: Lack of planning increases the likelihood and severity of losses.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses serving cannabis or controlled substances.
restrictions.why: Controlled substances are not insurable under standard commercial policies.

preferred: Businesses performing non-motorized window treatment installations using trained and certified personnel (ensures compliance and reduces risk).
Operations with documented proof of staff training programs in installation and safety standards (demonstrates commitment to safety and quality).
Firms using only direct employees for installation and repair work (greater control over quality and liability).
Businesses maintaining active relationships with reputable, established vendors and manufacturers (reduces supply chain risk).
Firms utilizing CRM systems for customer management and scheduling (improves operational efficiency and reduces errors).
Operations that regularly conduct staff training on new products and installation techniques (keeps skills current and reduces accident risk).
Businesses providing residential and light commercial window treatments (lower exposure than heavy commercial or industrial).
Companies with a documented process for verifying subcontractor licensing and insurance (ensures compliance with coverage requirements).
Firms using Installation Floater coverage for products in transit (protects inventory and reduces claims).
Businesses that do not perform any electrical work beyond low-voltage systems for motorized blinds (limits electrical hazard exposure).
acceptable: Businesses using licensed and insured subcontractors for installation or repair work (provided documentation is maintained).
Firms installing motorized window treatments where all electrical work is performed by certified electricians or low-voltage technicians (meets regulatory and coverage requirements).
Operations offering both residential and commercial services, provided commercial work does not exceed 50% of total revenue (limits exposure to higher-risk environments).
Businesses with seasonal fluctuations in staffing, provided all temporary staff are trained and certified (maintains safety standards).
Firms purchasing directly from manufacturers and managing their own logistics (acceptable if proper transit coverage is in place).
Companies offering basic integration with home automation systems, provided only certified personnel perform the work (controls risk of improper installation).
Businesses operating in regions with moderate climate-related seasonality (acceptable if risk management practices are in place).
Firms providing minor repair services for window treatments, excluding major structural or electrical work (limits exposure to complex risks).
Operations with a mix of showroom and on-site consultation activities (acceptable if safety protocols are followed).
Businesses that use third-party logistics providers for product delivery, provided coverage is maintained during transit (ensures continuity of protection).
not_acceptable: Businesses installing or servicing motorized window treatments that integrate with home automation systems without certified electricians or low-voltage technicians (high electrical and liability risk).
Operations employing untrained or uncertified personnel for installation or repair work (increases risk of injury and claims).
Firms unable to provide proof of staff training or adherence to industry safety standards (lack of compliance undermines risk management).
Businesses using subcontractors who do not hold valid licenses or lack their own liability insurance (unacceptable transfer of risk).
Companies performing major electrical work or rewiring as part of window treatment installation (outside scope of acceptable risk).
Firms engaging in heavy commercial, industrial, or institutional installations (exceeds acceptable exposure for this class).
Businesses with a history of regulatory violations or non-compliance with installation standards (demonstrates poor risk profile).
Operations transporting window treatments without Installation Floater or equivalent transit coverage (unprotected inventory risk).
Companies offering repair or installation services for products not originally supplied or installed by them (increases product liability exposure).
Firms performing work in hazardous or high-security environments (e.g., correctional facilities, chemical plants) (unacceptable risk profile).
Businesses with no documented process for verifying subcontractor credentials (increases risk of uninsured losses).
Operations providing window treatment services as part of broader general contracting or remodeling activities (scope too broad for this class).
Businesses with more than 50% of revenue from commercial or industrial clients (exceeds acceptable exposure).
Firms with a pattern of claims related to improper installation or property damage (demonstrates ongoing risk issues).
Companies offering integration with high-voltage or complex automation systems beyond standard window treatments (outside appetite).

restrictions.rule: Installation activities must be performed by trained and certified personnel.
restrictions.why: Ensures compliance with safety standards and reduces risk of improper installation.

restrictions.rule: Proof of training programs and adherence to industry safety standards is mandatory for coverage.
restrictions.why: Demonstrates commitment to quality and regulatory compliance.

restrictions.rule: Use of subcontractors for installation or repair work is permitted only if they hold valid licenses.
restrictions.why: Prevents liability from unqualified or unlicensed workers.

restrictions.rule: Subcontractors must carry their own liability insurance to qualify for coverage.
restrictions.why: Ensures risk is not transferred to the primary insured.

restrictions.rule: Coverage excludes installation or servicing of motorized window treatments that integrate with home automation systems unless performed by certified electricians or low-voltage technicians.
restrictions.why: Reduces exposure to electrical hazards and complex integration risks.

restrictions.rule: Installation Floater coverage is required for window treatments and blinds while in transit.
restrictions.why: Protects inventory and reduces risk of loss or damage during transportation.

restrictions.rule: Major electrical work or rewiring as part of installation is not covered.
restrictions.why: Such work falls outside the expertise and risk appetite for this business class.

restrictions.rule: Work in hazardous or high-security environments is excluded.
restrictions.why: These settings present elevated and unmanageable risks.

restrictions.rule: Repair or installation of products not originally supplied or installed by the business is excluded.
restrictions.why: Increases product liability and complicates claims handling.

restrictions.rule: Businesses must maintain documentation of subcontractor credentials and insurance.
restrictions.why: Ensures ongoing compliance and facilitates claims processing.

preferred: Custom woodworking projects with documented safety protocols and dust control systems in place (minimizes fire and health risks)
Carpentry businesses operating exclusively on non-structural interior projects (lower liability exposure)
Workshops with modern, well-maintained equipment and regular safety inspections (reduces accident frequency)
Businesses with no on-site finishing using flammable chemicals (limits fire hazard)
Operations with written employee safety training and PPE requirements (demonstrates risk management)
Carpentry businesses with less than 5 employees and no subcontracted labor (simplifies risk profile)
Woodworking shops located in commercial zones with compliant fire suppression systems (meets code requirements)
Businesses sourcing materials from certified, reputable suppliers (reduces supply chain issues)
Workshops with separate, ventilated finishing areas (improves air quality and fire safety)
Carpentry businesses with no exterior or roofing work (avoids height and weather risks)
acceptable: General carpentry businesses performing both residential and commercial work with standard safety measures
Workshops with a mix of hand and power tools, provided all equipment is regularly serviced
Businesses offering both design and build services for custom furniture and cabinetry
Carpentry businesses that occasionally perform on-site installations at customer locations
Operations with a small team (up to 10 employees) and documented hiring practices
Workshops located in mixed-use or light industrial areas with up-to-date occupancy permits
Businesses using water-based or low-VOC finishes for most projects
Carpentry businesses with a history of compliance with local building codes and permit requirements
Operations that subcontract specialized tasks (e.g., electrical, plumbing) to licensed professionals
Businesses with a documented process for customer consultations and project approvals
not_acceptable: Woodworking or carpentry businesses engaged in large-scale structural construction or framing (high liability)
Operations using highly flammable or toxic chemicals without proper ventilation or storage
Businesses with a history of OSHA violations or workplace safety citations
Workshops located in residential garages without proper zoning or fire protection
Carpentry businesses performing exterior work above two stories (increased fall risk)
Operations lacking any employee safety training or written safety policies
Businesses with open-flame finishing or heat treatment processes on-site
Workshops with significant combustible dust accumulation and no dust extraction system
Carpentry businesses that manufacture or install playground equipment or other high-liability products
Operations with more than 20 employees and no dedicated HR or risk management staff
Businesses with a record of unresolved customer complaints or legal disputes
Workshops operating in flood-prone or wildfire-prone areas without mitigation plans
Carpentry businesses that regularly perform demolition or hazardous material removal
Operations with significant off-site storage of lumber or chemicals in unsecured locations
Businesses that do not carry required local or state licenses for construction or carpentry work

restrictions.rule: No acceptance for businesses performing structural framing or load-bearing construction.
restrictions.why: Structural work carries significantly higher liability and risk of catastrophic loss.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for operations using flammable or toxic finishing chemicals without compliant ventilation and storage.
restrictions.why: Improper chemical handling increases fire and health hazards.

restrictions.rule: Workshops must have documented safety protocols and employee training.
restrictions.why: Lack of safety procedures leads to higher accident rates and claims.

restrictions.rule: No acceptance for businesses with a record of OSHA violations in the past three years.
restrictions.why: Recent safety violations indicate ongoing risk management issues.

restrictions.rule: Workshops must be located in properly zoned commercial or industrial spaces with up-to-date fire protection.
restrictions.why: Improper zoning and inadequate fire safety increase risk of regulatory action and loss.

restrictions.rule: No acceptance for businesses performing exterior work above two stories.
restrictions.why: Work at height increases fall and injury risk.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for businesses manufacturing playground equipment or other products intended for children.
restrictions.why: Children’s products carry elevated liability and regulatory scrutiny.

restrictions.rule: No acceptance for businesses with more than 20 employees unless dedicated risk management is demonstrated.
restrictions.why: Larger operations require formal risk controls to manage exposures.

restrictions.rule: No acceptance for businesses with unresolved legal disputes or outstanding regulatory actions.
restrictions.why: Legal and regulatory issues signal ongoing operational risk.

restrictions.rule: No coverage for operations in areas with high wildfire or flood risk unless mitigation measures are in place.
restrictions.why: Environmental hazards can lead to catastrophic property loss.
